catalogue: Australian livable-housing access, entrance, circulation, sanitary and future-adaptation construction

objects.name: livable-housing physical construction system
objects.definition: The coordinated physical paths, entrances, doorways, corridors, sanitary construction, step-free shower and concealed wall reinforcement used to make a dwelling easier to enter, use and adapt.
functions: Provide a step-free route to and into the dwelling
Support unimpeded movement through nominated internal routes
Provide sanitary and shower construction that can be adapted with less demolition

ncc_references.relationship: Coordinates the physical construction used for livable-housing access, circulation, sanitary use and future adaptation.

cad.pattern: Connected route and nominated adaptable rooms
cad.placement: From an allotment, parking or attached-garage origin through the dwelling
cad.opening: Uses measured clear openings and circulation envelopes without turning them into solids
cad.load: Pedestrian, fixture, wall-lining and future grabrail actions transferred to supporting construction

notes: The ABCB Standard is not intended to achieve equivalence with AS 1428.1. Adoption, exemptions and local alternatives are jurisdiction and project metadata.

objects.name: step-free dwelling access assembly
objects.definition: The continuous physical route from an accepted origin to a nominated dwelling entrance, assembled from path, ramp or step-ramp surfaces, landings, gates, drainage and the connected entrance construction without an intervening step.
functions: Connect the access origin to the entrance
Coordinate slopes, landings, gates, drainage and the entrance threshold
not_synonyms: AS 1428.1 continuous accessible path of travel automatically

ncc_references.document: ABCB Standard for Livable Housing Design
ncc_references.relationship: Defines the route options and constraints for Class 1a step-free dwelling access.

cad.pattern: One continuous trafficable route with segmented gradient and surface fields
cad.placement: Between access origin and nominated entrance
cad.start: Allotment entry, garage, carport or exclusive parking
cad.opening: Preserves clear passage around posts, piers, vehicles, gate leaves and door swings
cad.load: Walking actions and any suspended-path loads delivered to ground or supporting frame

notes: Step-free is a property of the complete connected route; it is not a paving material or a hidden layer.

objects.name: allotment-boundary-to-entrance step-free access assembly
objects.definition: A step-free dwelling access route beginning at the pedestrian entry at the allotment boundary and ending at the nominated entrance.
functions: Connect adjoining ground-level pedestrian entry to the dwelling
Provide a continuous route across the site
Coordinate gates, paths, ramps and arrival landing

cad.pattern: Site route from boundary opening to dwelling
cad.opening: Gate and pinch-point clearances remain measurable
cad.load: Trafficable surface supported by ground or local structure

objects.name: attached-garage or carport step-free access assembly
objects.definition: A step-free route from an appurtenant attached garage or carport to a compliant connecting entrance door into the dwelling.
functions: Provide sheltered step-free entry from vehicle storage
Connect the parking or set-down area directly to the dwelling
Coordinate floor levels, fire separation, weather and door threshold construction

cad.pattern: Clear route beside or beyond parked vehicle
cad.placement: Within attached garage or carport and at connecting door
cad.opening: Preserves route beside structural piers, stored vehicle and door swing
cad.load: Pedestrian path carried by garage slab or floor

notes: The connecting door can be the nominated entrance; another front door does not automatically need the same H8 entrance role.

objects.name: exclusive-parking-to-entrance step-free access assembly
objects.definition: A step-free route from a car parking space provided for the exclusive use of dwelling occupants to the nominated entrance door.
functions: Provide a clear pedestrian route around the parked vehicle
Coordinate parking surface, path and entrance levels

cad.pattern: Parking rectangle connected to pedestrian route
cad.placement: On allotment between vehicle access and entrance
cad.opening: Vehicle, posts, walls and stored items remain obstructions
cad.load: Vehicle and pedestrian actions carried by hardstand

objects.name: step-free pedestrian path assembly
objects.definition: The trafficable path surface, substrate, edges, joints and drainage forming a non-ramp or ramped segment of the step-free dwelling access route.
functions: Provide a firm continuous walking surface
Follow the designed route and levels
Drain surface water without creating a step

cad.pattern: Continuous strip following site route
cad.placement: On ground or supported above it
cad.opening: Clear width is checked between actual edges and projections
cad.load: Trafficable surface transfers actions to substrate, ground or frame

notes: Path, ramp and step ramp are geometry classes with different constraints; they may use similar materials.

objects.name: paved step-free access path assembly
objects.definition: A ground-supported step-free path made with concrete, unit paving or another firm paved surface over prepared substrate and edge restraint.
functions: Distribute walking actions to prepared ground

cad.pattern: Ground-following paved strip
cad.opening: Joints, covers and drains stay flush with trafficable face
cad.load: Surface and base distribute pedestrian actions to subgrade

objects.name: concrete step-free access path assembly
objects.definition: A formed and finished concrete strip or slab providing a ground-supported step-free access path, including joints, thickened edges or reinforcement where selected.

cad.pattern: Segmented concrete strip with transverse joints
cad.opening: Drains and service covers remain flush and coordinated
cad.load: Slab distributes actions to ground

objects.name: unit-paved step-free access path assembly
objects.definition: A step-free path surfaced with concrete, clay or stone paving units laid over a prepared bedding and base with restrained edges.
functions: Accommodate site layout and local replacement
Transfer walking actions through bedding to the base

cad.pattern: Repeated paving units clipped to path boundary
cad.opening: Unit joints and service covers remain within surface tolerance
cad.load: Unit and bedding distribute pedestrian actions

objects.name: raised deck or boardwalk step-free access path assembly
objects.definition: A suspended step-free path made from trafficable boards or panels over joists, bearers, posts or another framed support system.
functions: Carry the route above finished ground
Bridge site level or drainage conditions
Provide an open or permeable walking surface

cad.pattern: Parallel boards over framed linear supports
cad.placement: Suspended above ground along access route
cad.opening: Board gaps, service penetrations and edge clearances are explicit
cad.load: Decking to joists, bearers, posts and footings

objects.name: single step-ramp assembly on a livable access path
objects.definition: One short sloping trafficable construction used to overcome a single local level difference within the step-free dwelling access route.
functions: Replace one local step with a slope
Connect adjacent path or landing levels

cad.pattern: One short planar slope between adjacent levels
cad.placement: At a single local level change on access route
cad.opening: Clear width maintained across entire slope
cad.load: Trafficable surface transfers to ground or local support

notes: The step ramp is a distinct geometry class from a longer access ramp and from a ramped threshold contained within a door jamb.

objects.name: livable-access ramp landing assembly
objects.definition: A level or drainage-falled trafficable platform at the end of a ramp segment on the step-free dwelling access route.
functions: Provide level transition between ramp segments
Connect ramp, path and entrance surfaces
Support turning or resting movement where designed

cad.pattern: Planar platform at ramp termination
cad.placement: At each end of access ramp
cad.opening: Clear of posts, gate leaf and unrelated door swing
cad.load: Trafficable surface through substrate to ground or frame

objects.name: gate assembly within a step-free dwelling access path
objects.definition: A pedestrian gate, its posts, hinges, latch, stops and ground interface located within the step-free access route while preserving the required clear opening and threshold condition.

cad.pattern: Hinged or sliding leaf between gate posts
cad.opening: Clear opening measured with leaf fully open
cad.load: Leaf actions through hinges, posts and footings

objects.name: exclusive-use parking space incorporated into livable access
objects.definition: The unobstructed vehicle standing surface and connected pedestrian departure area used as an origin or part of the required step-free access route.
functions: Provide space to leave the vehicle and join the access path
Maintain usable surface levels around fixed construction

cad.pattern: Rectangular hardstand with adjoining departure route
cad.opening: Structural columns, brick piers and storage are explicit obstructions
cad.load: Vehicle actions through pavement to ground

notes: This is not automatically an AS 2890 accessible parking bay; it belongs to the selected H8 Class 1a route.

objects.name: livable step-free dwelling entrance assembly
objects.definition: A nominated dwelling entrance composed of its door or door set, frame, clear opening, threshold construction, arrival landing and any external weatherproofing needed to preserve step-free entry.
functions: Provide level or suitably ramped entry into the dwelling
Connect the external access route to the internal floor
Coordinate door operation, clear passage, weather, drainage and termite interfaces

ncc_references.document: ABCB Standard for Livable Housing Design
ncc_references.relationship: Defines the clear opening, threshold, landing and weatherproofing construction for the nominated entrance.

cad.pattern: Door opening crossing wall with aligned inside and outside trafficable surfaces
cad.opening: Clear opening calculated from installed leaf, frames and operating position
cad.load: Door actions to frame; walking and drainage actions to landing and floor

notes: Door leaf width is not the same as clear opening width. The selected entrance need not be the architectural front door.

objects.name: external arrival landing at a livable entrance
objects.definition: The external trafficable landing immediately on the arrival side of the nominated entrance door, coordinated with the access path, threshold, door swing and drainage.
functions: Provide stable arrival space before entry
Drain water without obstructing the doorway

cad.pattern: External planar platform aligned to doorway
cad.opening: Required landing field excludes structural posts and unrelated obstructions
cad.load: Trafficable surface transfers to ground or framing

objects.name: external step-free entrance weatherproofing assembly
objects.definition: The coordinated drainage, permeable-surface or roof-cover construction used to manage water at an external step-free entrance without introducing an unacceptable threshold step.
functions: Limit water entry at low threshold
Drain the landing and door sill interface
Coordinate access, weatherproofing, termite inspection and bushfire requirements

cad.pattern: Drainage and cover components surrounding low doorway threshold
cad.start: Landing outer edge or roof drip line
cad.opening: Drain grates, deck gaps and inspection access remain explicit
cad.load: Walking, water and roof actions transferred through their separate supports

notes: A level access line and weatherproofing must be solved together; deleting the sill upstand is not a complete detail.

objects.name: channel-drained step-free entrance assembly
objects.definition: An entrance weatherproofing arrangement using a linear drain across the width of an impermeable external landing near the door sill.
functions: Intercept surface water approaching the sill
Convey collected water to an outfall

cad.pattern: Linear channel crossing full entrance width
cad.placement: In impermeable landing outside door sill
cad.opening: Grate slots and removable access remain trafficable
cad.load: Grate carries foot traffic; channel conveys water to outlet

objects.name: permeable raised-deck step-free entrance assembly
objects.definition: A step-free entrance landing made with gapped trafficable decking over a separately drained surface or space below.
functions: Allow water through the trafficable layer
Preserve level entry at the sill
Direct water below the landing away from the building

cad.pattern: Gapped deck surface over drained lower plane
cad.opening: Board gaps and drainage outlet are explicit
cad.load: Deck boards to joists and frame; water to lower drainage surface

objects.name: roof-covered step-free entrance assembly
objects.definition: A nominated step-free entrance protected by a roof or canopy over the arrival area, with the roof supports and drainage kept outside the required path and landing space.
functions: Reduce direct rain exposure at the entrance
Protect the arrival landing and sill
Coordinate roof drainage without obstructing access

cad.pattern: Small roof plane over entrance landing
cad.placement: Above external arrival side of entrance
cad.opening: Posts and columns stay outside route and landing clear fields
cad.load: Roof actions to wall, beams, posts and footings

notes: Roof cover reduces exposure but does not erase the need to coordinate sill, surface falls and the selected drainage path.

objects.name: internal livable-housing circulation assembly
objects.definition: The connected ground- or entry-level floor route, corridors, hallways, passageways and nominated doorways providing movement to the relevant habitable rooms, laundry, sanitary compartment, shower and attached garage or carport.
functions: Maintain clear passage between finished wall surfaces
Coordinate door openings, swings, thresholds and fixed obstructions

ncc_references.document: ABCB Standard for Livable Housing Design
ncc_references.relationship: Defines which doorways and connecting corridors carry the livable internal-circulation role.

cad.pattern: Connected floor strip and door graph through nominated rooms
cad.placement: Within dwelling from entrance to relevant destinations
cad.end: Relevant rooms, sanitary compartment and shower
cad.opening: Widths derive from actual finished walls and installed door positions
cad.load: Normal floor and wall actions; route itself is a spatial relationship

notes: Clear passage and circulation overlays may be displayed, but the physical model remains the floor, walls, doors, frames, thresholds and fixed joinery.

objects.name: livable-housing internal doorway assembly
objects.definition: An internal wall opening with its frame, door leaf or panels, operating hardware and threshold or floor transition, selected and installed to provide the required clear passage on a nominated internal route.
functions: Open and close a room boundary
Provide measured clear passage when fully open
Coordinate door operation with corridor and room circulation

cad.pattern: Door set within wall opening with explicit open state
cad.opening: Calculated from installed frame, stops, leaf thickness, panel overlap and fully open position
cad.load: Door self-weight and operation to frame and wall

notes: A nominal 820 mm leaf does not automatically produce an 820 mm clear opening.

objects.name: livable-housing sanitary compartment assembly
objects.definition: The nominated ground- or entry-level room or space containing a toilet pan, its surrounding finished walls, doorway, fixed fixtures and future-grabrail supporting construction arranged for independent approach and use.
functions: Maintain usable space around and in front of the toilet pan
Provide walls capable of later grabrail installation

ncc_references.document: ABCB Standard for Livable Housing Design
ncc_references.relationship: Defines the selected entry-level sanitary compartment and constraints around the toilet pan.

cad.pattern: Room enclosure around pan, fixtures and doorway
cad.placement: Ground or entry level of dwelling
cad.opening: Door swing and fixed fixtures are tested against circulation overlay
cad.load: Fixture loads to floor and wall; future grabrail loads to reinforced wall

notes: Sanitary compartment names the room or space containing the pan, not the ceramic fixture itself.

objects.name: livable-housing hobless step-free shower access assembly
objects.definition: The nominated shower entry, floor levels, water-retaining edge, drainage, screen arrangement and surrounding wall construction providing both a hobless and step-free crossing.
functions: Retain and drain water while avoiding a hob
Coordinate wall reinforcement for future grabrails

ncc_references.document: ABCB Standard for Livable Housing Design
ncc_references.relationship: Requires one selected shower entry to be both hobless and step-free while retaining wet-area compliance.

cad.pattern: Continuous floor crossing into drained shower field
cad.opening: Entry lip, screen base and door remain explicit
cad.load: Walking and fixture actions to floor; water to drainage; future grabrail actions to reinforced walls

notes: Hobless and step-free are independent conditions; the shower floor still falls to drainage.

objects.name: future-grabrail wall reinforcement system
objects.definition: Concealed structural sheeting, timber noggings, light-gauge steel noggings or metal plate incorporated into selected bathroom and sanitary walls so a later grabrail can be fixed with less removal of wall lining.
functions: Provide a future fixing substrate behind wall lining
Spread grabrail actions into wall framing or solid construction
Preserve adaptable fixing zones around toilet, shower and bath

ncc_references.document: ABCB Standard for Livable Housing Design
ncc_references.relationship: Defines the selected fixture-adjacent reinforcement locations and permitted material families.

cad.pattern: Concealed sheet field or repeated horizontal backing members between studs
cad.placement: Behind lining on selected toilet, shower and bath walls
cad.opening: Coordinates door frames, windows, niches, services and cavity-slider pockets
cad.load: Future rail action through lining and fasteners into reinforcement and wall frame

notes: H8 requires the supporting construction, not installation of a grabrail. Concrete or masonry walls capable of supporting later rails may satisfy the role without added backing.

objects.name: step-free access path walking finish
objects.definition: The exposed trafficable finish on a livable access path, ramp, step ramp or landing, distinct from the slab, pavers, deck boards or other supporting substrate beneath it.
functions: Provide texture and weather exposure resistance
Receive slip-resistance evidence where the selected geometry requires it

cad.pattern: Continuous exposed face over path substrate
cad.placement: On access path, ramp or landing
cad.opening: Drains and covers finish flush as designed
cad.load: Foot traffic transferred into substrate

notes: A path can be a finished structural surface with no separately applied layer; create this object only when a distinct finish exists.

objects.name: step-free access path concrete slab
objects.definition: The ground-supported concrete slab forming the body and usually the exposed surface of a concrete livable access path.
functions: Bridge local ground irregularities and transfer actions to the base

cad.pattern: Continuous slab strip divided at joints
cad.placement: On compacted base along access route
cad.opening: Service covers and drains coordinate with slab openings
cad.load: Slab distributes pedestrian actions to base and ground

objects.name: step-free access path paving unit
objects.definition: One concrete, fired-clay or stone unit repeated to form the surface of a unit-paved livable access path.
functions: Allow patterned set-out and local replacement

cad.pattern: Repeated unit clipped at path edges and openings
cad.opening: Cut units surround drains, covers and posts
cad.load: Unit bearing through bedding to base

objects.name: access path paver bedding layer
objects.definition: The levelled sand, mortar or proprietary bedding layer directly supporting paving units on a livable access path.
functions: Establish the final surface plane and falls

cad.pattern: Continuous thin layer below pavers
cad.opening: Stops at drains, slabs and rigid edge restraints
cad.load: Paver loads distributed to base

objects.name: step-free access path compacted base layer
objects.definition: The compacted granular or stabilised layer below a paved path slab, bedding or surface that provides a stable formation and distributes loads to subgrade.
functions: Provide a trimmed platform at the designed route and falls

cad.pattern: Continuous formation strip below path
cad.opening: Services and drains interrupt or penetrate the base
cad.load: Surface loads spread to subgrade

objects.name: paved access path edge restraint
objects.definition: A continuous kerb, concrete haunch, rigid strip or anchored edging that confines paving and protects the side of a ground-supported step-free path.
functions: Protect bedding and base from erosion

cad.pattern: Linear profile following path edge
cad.placement: At one or both sides of paved path
cad.opening: Breaks for drainage and transitions
cad.load: Lateral paving pressure and edge impacts to ground or anchors

notes: An edge restraint is not automatically an upstand required for an accessible ramp; store the selected role separately.

objects.name: concrete access path movement-joint assembly
objects.definition: A formed separation in a concrete path slab with joint filler, sealant, dowel or other selected load-transfer and edge detail while maintaining a trafficable surface.

cad.pattern: Transverse or longitudinal joint across slab
cad.opening: Joint width remains a measured surface discontinuity
cad.load: Movement accommodated; dowels transfer selected actions

objects.name: step-free boardwalk decking board
objects.definition: One trafficable timber or composite board repeated across a raised livable access path or permeable entrance landing.
functions: Permit drainage through controlled joints between boards

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel boards with explicit gaps
cad.opening: Joints and cut-outs are explicit and checked at trafficable surface
cad.load: Board spans to joists

objects.name: step-free boardwalk joist
objects.definition: A repeated horizontal or sloping timber or steel member directly supporting decking boards in a raised access path.
functions: Transfer loads to bearers, ledgers or beams

cad.pattern: Repeated linear supports below deck boards
cad.opening: Trimmers frame openings for drains and posts
cad.load: Decking reactions to bearers

objects.name: step-free boardwalk bearer or beam
objects.definition: A primary horizontal or sloping member supporting boardwalk joists and transferring their reactions to posts, walls, ledgers or footings.
functions: Provide edge and intermediate support lines

cad.pattern: Primary linear support below joists
cad.placement: Along or across raised path frame
cad.opening: Splices and service clearances remain explicit
cad.load: Joist reactions to posts or foundations

objects.name: step-free boardwalk support post
objects.definition: A vertical timber, steel or concrete member supporting a raised access-path bearer or beam above a footing or other foundation element.

cad.pattern: Vertical supports at bearer stations
cad.opening: Posts remain outside required clear path where they project above surface
cad.load: Frame reactions into footing

objects.name: step-free boardwalk frame brace
objects.definition: A diagonal member, strap or framed element stabilising raised access-path posts, bearers or joists against lateral movement and racking.

cad.pattern: Diagonal between posts and beams or within frame plane
cad.opening: Keeps clear of drainage and services
cad.load: Tension or compression lateral action

objects.name: step-free boardwalk decking fixing
objects.definition: A screw, nail, clip or concealed fastening component securing an access-path decking board to its supporting joist.
functions: Maintain board spacing and surface alignment

cad.pattern: Repeated fixings at board-to-joist intersections
cad.placement: Through or beside decking into joist
cad.opening: Countersink remains flush with walking face where required
cad.load: Board restraint into joist

objects.name: under-deck entrance drainage surface
objects.definition: The sloping impermeable slab, tray, membrane or sheet below a permeable entrance deck that collects water passing through board gaps and directs it away from the building.
functions: Drain water away from the low entrance sill
Protect supporting construction or occupied space below

cad.pattern: Continuous lower plane below gapped decking
cad.placement: Between decking frame and structure or ground
cad.opening: Outlets and penetrations are sealed and explicit
cad.load: Water carried to outlet; layer supported by slab or framing

objects.name: step-free access path drainage channel
objects.definition: A linear surface-water drain alongside or across a livable access path, positioned and finished so its grate or opening does not create an unintended step or obstruction.
functions: Protect path and adjacent building from ponding

cad.pattern: Linear drain following or crossing path
cad.placement: At path low line or runoff interception point
cad.opening: Grate or slot is explicit at walking surface
cad.load: Foot traffic to grate and channel; water to outlet

objects.name: step-free access gate leaf
objects.definition: The moving framed, boarded, panelled or mesh portion of a pedestrian gate within the livable access route.
functions: Move clear of the required passage

cad.pattern: Moving panel within gate opening
cad.opening: Fully open position determines clear passage
cad.load: Self-weight and use actions to hinges or track

objects.name: step-free access gate post
objects.definition: A vertical structural member supporting gate hinges, guides or latch hardware at the side of a pedestrian access opening.
functions: Transfer gate actions to footing or fence structure

cad.pattern: Pair of vertical posts defining opening
cad.opening: Inside faces define available gate opening
cad.load: Gate and fence actions into footing

objects.name: step-free access gate hinge
objects.definition: A hinge or pivot connecting a swinging pedestrian gate leaf to its support post and controlling its rotational axis.

cad.pattern: Repeated connectors on gate pivot line
cad.opening: Hinge projection affects clear opening only where it intrudes
cad.load: Leaf self-weight and operational actions to post

objects.name: step-free access gate latch
objects.definition: A manually or automatically engaging fitting holding a pedestrian access gate leaf closed against its latch post.

cad.pattern: Latch body and keeper at gate edge
cad.opening: Handle projection may affect passage or operation
cad.load: Closing and wind actions into latch post

objects.name: step-free access gate stop
objects.definition: A floor-, post- or fence-mounted fitting limiting a gate leaf at its closed or fully open position without creating an unintended obstruction in the access path.
functions: Hold or locate leaf at selected position

cad.pattern: Small stop at leaf travel limit
cad.placement: On post, fence or outside clear walking line
cad.opening: Must not become an unmodelled trip obstruction
cad.load: Gate impact to support

objects.name: livable-access parking hardstand slab
objects.definition: The concrete or other rigid structural pavement forming the vehicle standing surface of an exclusive-use parking space incorporated into the step-free route.
functions: Maintain designed parking gradients and drainage

cad.pattern: Rectangular pavement field with joints
cad.opening: Columns, pits and drains are explicit
cad.load: Vehicle actions through slab to ground

objects.name: livable-access parking bituminous surface
objects.definition: A compacted asphalt or bituminous pavement surface forming the exclusive-use parking space and its pedestrian connection.
functions: Provide vehicle and pedestrian wearing surface
Drain to surrounding pavement or stormwater system

cad.pattern: Continuous pavement field
cad.opening: Drains and covers remain flush
cad.load: Vehicle and pedestrian actions to base

objects.name: exclusive parking space line marking
objects.definition: A painted or thermoplastic line on a parking surface identifying the intended vehicle standing boundary or pedestrian departure edge where marking is provided.
functions: Make the intended parking boundary visible
Identify the adjoining route where designed

cad.pattern: Painted line following selected parking boundary
cad.opening: No physical obstruction
cad.load: Non-structural coating

notes: Marking is optional physical paint; the required unobstructed parking geometry exists whether or not a line is painted.

objects.name: parking wheel stop
objects.definition: A low concrete, rubber or polymer member anchored to a parking surface to limit vehicle travel, treated as an obstruction when it projects into the usable parking or pedestrian route.

cad.pattern: Low transverse member at vehicle stop line
cad.opening: Must be included when testing the unobstructed parking and route geometry
cad.load: Vehicle tyre impact to anchors and pavement

objects.name: parking-to-step-free-path transition joint
objects.definition: The physical junction between a parking hardstand and the connected pedestrian access path, including changes in pavement material, joint fillers, edge profiles and drainage while maintaining the intended step-free crossing.

cad.pattern: Linear boundary between pavement fields
cad.placement: At parking-space departure to access path
cad.opening: Surface discontinuity remains measurable
cad.load: Traffic across joint into separate pavement systems

objects.name: livable-housing entrance doorset
objects.definition: The complete hinged, sliding, folding or multi-panel external door set selected as the step-free dwelling entrance, including leaf or panels, frame, hardware, seals and threshold.
functions: Provide the required clear entry passage when fully open
Coordinate weather sealing and low-threshold construction

cad.pattern: External door set within wall opening
cad.opening: Clear passage derives from fully installed and fully open configuration
cad.load: Door and wind actions through frame fixings to wall

objects.name: livable internal swing-door assembly
objects.definition: An internal doorway using one or more leaves rotating on side hinges or pivots, with the fully open leaf position used to establish clear passage.

cad.pattern: Rotating leaf within framed wall opening
cad.opening: Fully open leaf edge and frame determine clear width
cad.load: Leaf self-weight and use actions to hinges and frame

objects.name: livable surface-sliding internal door assembly
objects.definition: An internal door whose leaf or panel travels along the face of a wall on a top track or other guide rather than retracting into a wall cavity.
functions: Close the doorway without a swing arc
Keep the wall cavity available for services or reinforcement

cad.pattern: Panel translating parallel to wall face
cad.placement: Across internal wall opening with clear wall run beside it
cad.opening: Panel overlap, pull and frame determine clear width
cad.load: Panel self-weight through hangers to track and wall backing

objects.name: livable cavity-sliding internal door assembly
objects.definition: An internal sliding door set whose panel retracts into a framed wall pocket containing split studs, head track, guides and jamb components.
functions: Provide clear passage without a swing arc
Store the open door within the wall
Coordinate the pocket with wall lining, services and future-grabrail reinforcement

cad.pattern: Panel translating into wall pocket
cad.opening: Jambs, residual panel edge and handle determine clear width
cad.load: Panel to rollers and head track; linings and future rail loads to pocket frame and reinforcement

notes: Future grabrail fixings must not penetrate or obstruct the moving panel; pocket framing and backing require deliberate coordination.

objects.name: livable folding or concertina internal door assembly
objects.definition: An internal doorway closed by two or more hinged panels that fold and stack at one or both sides of the opening on pivots or a guide track.
functions: Fold panels into a compact stack
Provide clear passage based on the fully stacked position

cad.pattern: Linked panels folding to opening side
cad.opening: Folded panel stack is deducted from clear passage
cad.load: Panels through pivots, hinges and track to frame

objects.name: livable multi-panel stacking sliding door assembly
objects.definition: A doorway using multiple sliding panels that overlap or stack in the open position, with the resulting clear opening determined from the installed stack and frame.
functions: Slide panels into a stacked arrangement
Provide a measured opening larger than an individual panel
not_synonyms: clear opening automatically equal to frame width

cad.pattern: Multiple panels translating on parallel tracks
cad.placement: At nominated internal or entrance doorway
cad.opening: Installed panel stack and frame determine passage
cad.load: Panels to rollers, tracks and frame

objects.name: internal doorway door leaf
objects.definition: A solid, hollow-core, panelled or glazed moving leaf that swings or slides to close a livable internal doorway.
functions: Carry handle, latch, hinges or hangers
Move clear to form the passage
attributes: fire or acoustic evidence if applicable

cad.pattern: Rectangular moving panel
cad.placement: Within internal door frame or track
cad.opening: Leaf thickness and open position affect clear width
cad.load: Self-weight through hinges or rollers

objects.name: internal sliding door panel
objects.definition: A moving internal door panel configured to translate along a wall face or into a wall cavity on hangers, rollers and guides.
functions: Travel into its open parking position
Carry pulls, edge latch and roller hardware

cad.pattern: Rectangular panel translating horizontally
cad.opening: Residual leading edge and handle projection affect passage
cad.load: Panel to hangers and track

objects.name: internal folding door panel
objects.definition: One narrow leaf within a linked set of internal folding or concertina door panels.
functions: Form part of the closed door field
Transfer actions through hinges and pivots

cad.pattern: Linked narrow panels
cad.opening: Stacked panels occupy part of opening
cad.load: Panel actions through hinges, pivots and track

objects.name: internal doorway frame
objects.definition: The installed head and jamb frame surrounding an internal door opening and receiving stops, hinges, guides, latch hardware and architraves.
functions: Line and define the wall opening
Provide finished opening faces used in clear-width measurement

cad.pattern: Three-sided frame within wall opening
cad.opening: Inside faces and stops bound nominal opening
cad.load: Door hardware actions through frame fixings to wall

objects.name: internal door frame head
objects.definition: The horizontal top member of an internal door frame spanning between jambs and carrying stops or sliding-track interfaces where selected.
functions: Complete the top of the frame

cad.pattern: Horizontal frame member above door
cad.opening: Lower face and stop define clear height
cad.load: Hardware and frame actions to jambs and wall

objects.name: internal door frame jamb
objects.definition: One vertical side member of an internal door frame, serving hinge, latch, guide, pocket-return or closing roles according to the door type.
functions: Define the side of the doorway
Carry hinges, strike or guide hardware
Provide the finished face used in opening measurement

cad.pattern: Vertical frame member at opening side
